# Jordan Ellis: missed calls at Ellis Plumbing (14 Oct 2026)

[[sources/historical_calls/2026-10-14-jordan-ellis-intro-call-4bbd735b/INDEX|Source index]] · [[sources/intake/records/4bbd735bd750c2a6cee5b5669f8a0ceb8a5b2e2dd9eb077a71ba698b55911111|Original]] · Lines L7-L17
Attributed historical evidence, not canonical TTROS truth.

## Summary
Jordan says calls go unanswered when everyone is out on jobs, and voicemail is only checked at the end of the day. He doesn't know how many calls are missed. Liam proposed measuring before changing anything, and Jordan agreed.

## Points
- **Jordan Ellis:** nobody answers the phone when everyone is on jobs (L8).
- **Jordan Ellis:** Priya checks voicemail at the end of the day, by which time callers have gone elsewhere (L9).
- **Jordan Ellis:** missed calls are not tracked; his guess is ten to thirty a week (L11).
- **Jordan Ellis:** callers who leave a message get a call back next morning; those who don't are lost (L14-L15).
- **Liam Duff:** suggested measuring missed calls first (L16).
- **Jordan Ellis:** doesn't like paying for things he can't see working (L17).

## Commitments and open loops
- None stated.

## Key quotes
> "If they don't leave a message, it's just gone." (Jordan Ellis, L15)

## Caveats
The ten-to-thirty figure is Jordan's guess, not a measurement (L11).
